title: Low degree mass outside a coordinate set
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses, let $f$ be a real-valued function on its outcome space, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. Suppose $0\le\rho\le1$ and $\tau\ge0$, every coordinate $i\notin J$ has influence at most $\tau$, and for every coordinate $i$ the sum of $\rho^{|S|}\mathbb E_P f_S^2$ over coordinate sets $S$ containing $i$ is at most $I_i(f)^{3/2}$. Then $\rho^k$ times the sum of $\mathbb E_P f_S^2$ over sets $S$ with $|S|\le k$ that are not contained in $J$ is at most $\sqrt{\tau}\,I(f)$, where $f_S$ denotes the $S$-component, $I_i(f)$ the coordinate influence, and $I(f)$ the total influence.

$f$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
